text: Before Sevilla, Raphinha had already scored a hat-trick against Racing Santander. After Sevilla, it was twelve league goals in seven matches. Barcelona had won all seven league games and their opening Champions League match against Feyenoord. Those numbers earn the headlines, but Sevilla gives us a more revealing sequence. The home side pressed aggressively and took the lead. Barcelona did not simply pile on goals from the opening whistle. They had to find a way through an opponent prepared to disturb them. On the equalizer, Christensen sends a pass through the center. Raphinha does not wait in the old winger's lane. He runs directly at the gap, shifts past his marker, and finishes. The goal starts before the shot, when the back line is forced to decide who owns the space he has entered. It is worth watching the defenders rather than the celebration on this replay. As the pass travels, the nearest man turns toward goal; that half-second of uncertainty is precisely the space Raphinha wants.
